title: The host payload ships the installed read handler and an installed-implementation catalog; `ia host` records a join and `ia doctor` reports both
summary: @inventarch/cli's embedded host payload now carries @inventarch/agent-composition-system and its dependency closure as a payload root, inside the payload and not as a CLI or distribution source dependency (the separate runner app statically imports its reviewed runtime exports), plus a generated, inventoried implementations.json in format ia.installed-implementations.v1. Shipping the handler adds 174 files, roughly 360 KB of payload and 80 KB of archive; the exact figures move with every payload build. The catalog's evaluators section is an ia-evaluator-catalog/1.0 value with no installed entries, the built-ins being implicit; its operations section lists captured-source-read-v1 as available with its descriptor version, operation identity authoring-system/binding/operation/read-captured-source, handler ia.captured-source.read.v1, input and output validator ids, the payload path of the shipped handler module (agent-composition-system's dist/installed-read.js), that module's SHA-256 and the installed packages of its closure. The payload builder imports that declaration module at build time to read the declaration; it finds an implementation package only in the repository's own node_modules, and lists one unavailable, with the reason and never as available, when its package is not installed there, its handler module is not built, or the module imports a file that is not shipped or a package outside its shipped package closure. @inventarch/db's @inventarch/db/distribution entrypoint, and the new @inventarch/db/internal/distribution/implementations subpath, add checkInstalledImplementations(value), INSTALLED_IMPLEMENTATIONS_FORMAT and the AvailableOperation, UnavailableOperation, RevokedOperation, InstalledOperation, InstalledImplementationsValue and InstalledImplementationsCheck types: the catalog's one shape, whose operation rows are available, unavailable or revoked (with a reason; nothing produces a revoked row yet). checkInstalledImplementations copies its input once as plain data (refusing a proxy, accessor, class instance, cycle or excess size) and returns the checked copy deeply frozen. @inventarch/distribution adds the ./implementations subpath (and ./internal/implementations), exporting readInstalledImplementations(directory, release, verify?), installedImplementationsValue, readJoins, joinHost and leaveHost with their types, re-exporting the db shape, and INSTALLED_IMPLEMENTATIONS, INSTALLED_IMPLEMENTATIONS_ID, JOINS and JOINS_FORMAT; @inventarch/distribution/host-observe adds hostVerifier(), the HostVerifier type and verifierOf(verify?), and observeHosts gains a third parameter and readInstalledState a verify option, each taking a HostVerifier: a memo of verifyHostCache that one report shares, which only hostVerifier makes, so any other function passed there is ignored and the payload is verified afresh (a public reader always verifies); verifyHostCache now also returns the verified inventory's files and version, and otherwise verifies as before; probeContextHookImplementation reads only the verified cache's launcher and is typed for that alone, so a value of the 2.0.0 verified-cache shape still type-checks. readInstalledImplementations first verifies the whole payload as verifyHostCache does and requires it to verify as the given release, so a file the inventory does not list (anywhere inside the payload directory; nothing outside it is verified, and the closure check follows literal import specifiers only), a link or junction, a missing file or changed bytes refuse with that verification's code and nothing is read from it; the catalog is the file the verified inventory lists, read again against its pin; an available operation whose handler module or a closure package manifest the inventory does not list is unavailable, and one whose handler digest disagrees with the inventory refuses with IA-DIST-INTEGRITY-MISMATCH. What binds is the handler module's digest with the verified inventory, which pins every other byte of the closure; the composition descriptor's implementationDigest is not recorded. A v1 payload, or a v2 payload whose inventory lists no catalog (every payload built before this change, including the one 2.0.0 ships), reads as unavailable rather than damaged. joinHost records, under the host lock with the pending-journal check made under it, one row per consumer in .ia/distributions/hosts/joins.json (format ia.host-joins.v1: consumer, implementation installed-implementations, payload version, catalog digest, payload release and consumer revision), derived from the committed <host>-workspace.json registration and the catalog of the payload it names, and drops that row when there is no registration or no catalog; receipts that cannot be read refuse rather than being replaced. ia host claude|codex --apply, and so ia init --host, reads the receipts before writing anything, refusing ones it cannot read with the repair of deleting them, and records the host's join after every element is applied, with the workspace's authored revision as the consumer revision; a removal drops it, and a failure there names the rerun that finishes the set, so an interrupted apply leaves no join or the previous one. ia doctor adds an implementations row for the catalog of the payload this installation pins in the IA home (ok when present, warn when it lists an unavailable or revoked operation, info when the payload carries none or is not materialized, fail when the payload fails verification) and one join-<host> row per recorded join, compared through the trust ia validate binds with (ok when it names the catalog of the payload this installation pins in the IA home and the host's registration names exactly that payload, warn when it is drifted, when the registration names another release or another directory or spelling, which is never opened, or when the host is not registered, unknown when that payload cannot be read or verified or the installation pins none), an info row for a registered host with no join and a fail row for receipts that cannot be read; one verification of each payload serves its host, catalog and join rows, and doctor still writes nothing. Limits: catalog inspection and CLI/distribution projection do not execute installed evaluators or operation handlers. The separate local runner host executes its fixed installed captured-read operation under the selected mandate and bounded runtime; `@check` binding against the evaluators section is described in the check-binding-evidence note; the catalog lists no installed evaluator; a join records which catalog a host registration joined, not that any handler ran; the ia host --json envelope and its human output are unchanged.
